extracted.intended_audience: hospitals, hospital quality/reporting staff, and other stakeholders participating in or commenting on the CJR-X model (CMS rulemaking audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for selecting, reporting, scoring, and displaying quality measures in the CMS CJR-X episode payment model, including measure definitions, data submission pathways, percentile assignment, composite score construction, and how quality performance affects payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Visits within 7 Days of HOPD Surgery (OP-36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses quality of care following surgery or cystoscopy in hospital outpatient settings by measuring any of: (1) an inpatient admission directly after the surgery; or (2) an unplanned hospital visit (inpatient admission, observation stay, or ED visit) occurring after discharge or within 7 days of the surgery. Score is a ratio of predicted to expected number of post-surgical hospital visits given HOPD case mix and procedure mix (ratio <1 indicates fewer visits than expected; >1 indicates more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to capture early, unplanned utilization after outpatient procedures (including elective THA/TKA). Denominator = expected visits given case/procedure mix; numerator = predicted visits accounting for observed rate, number of surgeries, case mix, and procedure mix. CMS proposes inclusion in CJR-X outpatient measure set and seeks comment on its inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (HCAHPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: A standardized, national patient-experience survey producing 11 publicly reported measures (7 multi-item and 4 single-item measures) about patients' perceptions of their hospital experience. Administered to a random sample of adult inpatients 2 to 42 days after discharge; IPPS hospitals must achieve at least 300 completed surveys over four calendar quarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures domains such as communication with doctors and nurses, discharge information, responsiveness, cleanliness, and overall rating. Can be implemented in six survey modes; hospitals may use approved vendors or collect data if CMS-approved. CMS proposes using HCAHPS to assess inpatient episode quality in CJR-X, emphasizing standardized comparability and reduced additional reporting burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outpatient and Ambulatory Surgery CAHPS (OAS CAHPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient-experience survey for adults receiving care in Medicare-certified HOPDs and ASCs; outcomes are proportions of patients responding 'Yes' to survey questions about preparation, check-in, cleanliness, staff communication, discharge, and recovery instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures outpatient surgery patient experience domains (including information about what to do for side-effects). CMS proposes using OAS CAHPS to assess outpatient episode quality in CJR-X as the outpatient complement to HCAHPS and to avoid additional reporting burden by relying on existing outpatient quality reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital-Level THA/TKA Patient-Reported Outcome-Based Performance Measure (PRO-PM)
rubrics_metrics.description: A hospital-level PRO-PM that assesses change in patients' pain, physical function, and health-related quality of life before and after elective THA/TKA using instruments such as VR-12, PROMIS Global-10, HOOS Jr./KOOS Jr. (risk-adjusted to allow fair hospital comparisons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures outcomes that matter to beneficiaries (quality of life improvements) and complements utilization/complication measures. CMS proposes using the existing inpatient THA/TKA PRO-PM to assess LEJR episode quality for inpatient and outpatient episodes (without requiring outpatient PRO submission initially) and notes mandatory reporting timelines in HIQR/HOQR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use existing CMS reporting programs for data submission
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X would rely on data submission through existing CMS quality reporting programs (Hospital IQR for inpatient measures and Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program for outpatient measures) so participants do not submit additional data specifically for CJR-X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: Hospital-Level RSCR (CMIT #350), HCAHPS (CMIT #338), and THA/TKA PRO-PM (CMIT #1618) via Hospital IQR; Hospital Visits within 7 days (CMIT #344, OP-36) and OAS CAHPS (CMIT #162) via Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting. This is intended to minimize additional reporting burden for participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display of quality measures and public reporting timing
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X measure results will be publicly displayed on CMS Care Compare consistent with other publicly reported measures, with a 30-day preview period prior to public posting and approximately a 1-year lag before publishing PY1 measure scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will share each participant's quality metrics confidentially before public display. Measure performance periods may not align exactly with CJR-X performance years but will align with existing CMS reporting cadences to minimize burden and confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning measure performance via national percentile
rubrics_metrics.description: At reconciliation, assign each participant's measure point estimate to a performance percentile based on the national distribution of measure results for hospitals eligible for IPPS payment that meet minimum patient case or survey counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to the five proposed measures (RSCR, Hospital Visits within 7 days HOPD Surgery, HCAHPS, OAS CAHPS, THA/TKA PRO-PM). Measure-specific minimum case/survey thresholds are used to construct national distributions (referenced in Table X.C-02). CMS seeks comment on this percentile-based approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling non-reportable, new, or suppressed measure values (50th percentile assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any CJR-X participant without a reportable value for a measure, new hospitals identified as participants, or participants with a suppressed measure value due to calculation error will be assigned to the 50th performance percentile for that measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach is intended so that participants are not disadvantaged due to lack of applicable cases and to be consistent with CJR Model practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluding explicit quality improvement points from composite scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considered but is not proposing to include additional quality improvement points (e.g., awarding points for improvement of 2 deciles or more) in CJR-X's composite quality score; instead, scoring emphasizes absolute quality achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale includes emphasis on absolute clinical outcomes over short-term variation, administrative simplicity, predictability, alignment with TEAM (which does not include improvement points), and existing financial incentives for improvement through reconciliation structure. CMS seeks comment on not including improvement points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Score (CQS) concept and linkage to payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a composite quality score computed for each CJR-X participant summarizing performance across specified quality measures; the CQS links quality performance to the participant's discount factor and thereby affects reconciliation target prices and payment/repayment amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CQS allows each required measure to be meaningfully valued in a pay-for-performance methodology, incentivizing quality while tying financial opportunities to overall quality rather than individual measures alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality domains and domain weighting (complications, patient experience, PROs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose three quality domains—complications, patient experience, and patient-reported outcomes—and weight each domain: complications 50%, patient experience 40%, and PROs 10% for both inpatient and outpatient measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weights reflect clinical seriousness (complications), importance of communication and coordination (experience), and beneficiary-centered outcomes (PROs). These weights mirror the original CJR Model approach and account for outpatient measures by constructing separate inpatient and outpatient domain composites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure point-to-points decile scoring and small incremental point assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each measure point estimate is mapped to a performance percentile decile and assigned points according to proposed point values (small increments across deciles) that reflect the intended weight of the measure in the composite quality score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After determining point values per measure, CMS would sum points across inpatient measures to form the inpatient composite (capped at 20) and sum outpatient measure points to form the outpatient composite (also capped at 20). Specific point tables are referenced (Table X.C-04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capping inpatient and outpatient composite quality scores at 20 points
rubrics_metrics.description: The inpatient measure composite quality score and the outpatient composite quality score would each be capped at 20 points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cap mirrors the CJR Model design and standardizes the scale before weighting and combining into an overall composite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating the overall composite quality score by episode volume weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall composite quality score is the sum of the weighted average of the inpatient composite and outpatient composite quality scores, weighted by the hospital's proportion of inpatient to outpatient episodes, and the overall score is capped at 20 points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if 10% inpatient and 90% outpatient episode volume, overall CQS = (0.10 * inpatient_composite) + (0.90 * outpatient_composite). This approach accounts for each participant's episode mix when producing an overall quality score used to determine discount factors and payment adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aligning measure performance periods with existing CMS programs to minimize burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose measure performance periods that, where possible, align with existing CMS quality reporting program performance periods rather than CJR-X model performance years to avoid duplicative reporting and reduce participant burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that measure periods may not perfectly align with model performance years but asserts this is the least burdensome approach and similar to prior models (CJR, TEAM). Participants would receive measure data consistent with Care Compare schedules and existing program cadences.
